subject: Reserved capacity: GPU evaluation summary & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Singh <alex.singh@stor.ai>

Subject: Re: Intro + perf goals for Dedicated evaluation

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the call this morning — appreciate the deep dive. Quick confirmation of our targets so we can proceed with the sizing worksheet:

- Goals: 95th pct latency <= 250ms for interactive chat (streaming enabled). For non-streaming batch generation, p95 <= 350ms.
- Sustained throughput target: 8k tokens/sec across the pool during business peak.
- Peak concurrency: 40 concurrent user sessions; typical per-session concurrency is 6 active requests during typing bursts.
- Prompt mix: average prompt length ~220 input tokens, expected average generated tokens ~80. We attached a sample prompt distribution for accuracy.

We are comfortable with an initial 3-month reserved commitment if the validation run meets the SLOs and unit-cost targets. Please let us know what additional info you need.

Alex
Alex Singh
Head of Platform, StorAI
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>

Alex — thanks, this is perfect and matches what we heard on the call.

Action plan (short):
1) Internal sizing + GPU recommendation (this thread) — we’ll return a short matrix comparing A10G-like, A100 80GB, and H100 profiles for your workload plus expected reserved throughput and estimated cost/Tk. (target: 24 hrs)
2) Validation run: 48–72 hour soak against a dedicated pool with your sample prompt mix (we’ll need your sample distribution file — you mentioned attaching it)
3) Contracting: assuming validation passes, we’ll size a 3-month reserved capacity and provide a PO-ready quote.

Questions for you:
- Do you require strict KV-cache persistence between requests (sticky sessions) or is session-level caching sufficient?
- Any compliance constraints (e.g., on-prem keys) for the POC environment?

I’m looping engineering to produce the matrix. Karthik/Aditya — can you run the quick estimate below and flag any additional assumptions you want me to surface to Alex?

Thanks,
Kim

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>

Adding a few technical assumptions before I run numbers:

Assumptions (please confirm):
- Tokenization: byte-pair; average model tokens as Alex listed (input 220 / gen 80).
- Streaming: we’ll enable chunked streaming (server-side) — estimate ~8ms per token generation kernel overhead on A100/H100, ~12ms on A10G class.
- Precision: quantized int8 runtime available for MLP attention path — we’ll model both fp16 and int8.
- KV cache: session-level persistent cache is sufficient; full cross-session cache not required for correctness.

If those look right I’ll produce a matrix with: peak RPS equivalent, tokens/sec per GPU, p95 latency estimates (streaming vs non-streaming), and expected reserved throughput to guarantee SLOs with headroom (20%).

Karthik
Senior Infra Eng, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 30 Nov 2026 17:38:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity: GPU evaluation summary & next steps

I'm good with these assumptions. Quick notes from profiling earlier this quarter:
- H100 (with fp16 kernels) gives best tail latency for long sequences (>1024) — p95 improvements ~1.6x vs A100 in our tests. For your avg sequence (~300 total tokens), A100 and H100 p95 are closer, H100 still leads by ~20%.
- A10G-class (cost-effective) will likely meet p50 comfortably but struggles at p95 for concurrent bursts under streaming unless we increase reserved concurrency. Expect p95 delta ~2x vs A100 for bursty traffic.
- Int8 gives ~1.8x token/sec improvement on A100/H100 but regression risk on certain attention patterns; recommend fp16 for the POC and a later int8 pass after eval.

I’ll prepare the matrix with per-GPU tokens/sec and an estimate of how many GPUs to reserve to meet 8k tokens/sec with 20% headroom at p95.

—Aditya
SRE, Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Singh <alex.singh@stor.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 01 Dec 2026 08:05:00 -08:00
Subject: GPU evaluation matrix & recommended reserved throughput

Alex / Kim — attached is the evaluation matrix (gpu_evaluation_matrix.xlsx) and the short recommendation. Summary first:

- Recommendation (POC): 4 x A100-80GB nodes as the initial reserved pool. Rationale: balances predictable p95 latency, smoother streaming tails, and lower regression risk vs int8. Expected sustained tokens/sec per A100: ~2200 (fp16, your prompt mix). 4 GPUs -> ~8800 tokens/sec, with ~10% headroom.
- H100 alternative: 3 x H100 nodes would meet target (~3 x 3000 tokens/sec) and give better p95 (~20% lower); however list price + availability increases cost ~30% relative to A100 baseline.
- A10G-class: would require ~10 nodes to hit tokens/sec target; cost-effective at scale but operationally more variable at tail latencies. Not recommended for initial reserved pool if strict p95 SLOs matter.
- Streaming notes: with server-side chunked streaming and session-level KV cache, p95 streaming latency (per-token perceived) projected to be ~180–230ms on the A100 config above for the interactive case. Non-streaming generation p95 projected ~300ms.
- Suggested POC config: provision 4 x A100-80GB in Dedicated pool, enable fp16 kernels, enable KV session cache, run 72-hour soak with your prompt distribution.

Next steps we propose:
1) Alex: share the sample prompt distribution file and any compliance notes (KMS/HSM).
2) Redwood: schedule validation window (72 hours), pre-populate workload driver, share monitoring dashboard links and success criteria (p95 latency, error rate < 0.5%, cost/Tk target).
3) Contracting: Redwood to send provisional 3-month reserved quote based on 4 x A100.

I attached the matrix with per-GPU throughput numbers and cost estimates. Happy to hop on a quick call to talk tradeoffs.

Karthik
From: Alex Singh <alex.singh@stor.ai>

- Attached: storai_prompt_profile.json (sample prompt distribution and a few long-tail edge cases).

We can provision the validation window as soon as you confirm the H100 vs A100 per-GPU cost delta and a proposed validation start (we’re flexible next week).

Alex
